entries.note: Combined 46 mpg (US). EPA revised its fuel-economy methodology in 2008 and recalculated earlier cars, so this is the current estimate for a 2004 car, not the figure printed on the 2004 window sticker.

entries.publisher: US EPA / US Department of Energy

entries.title: 2018 Tesla Model 3 Long Range — EPA fuel economy record (vehicle 39836)
entries.publisher: US EPA / US Department of Energy
entries.note: EPA records the motor as 202 kW. Range 310 miles combined.

entries.title: 1994 Range Rover 4DR County Classic 4x4 — NHTSA Canadian Vehicle Specifications
entries.publisher: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
entries.note: vPIC's Canadian Vehicle Specifications endpoint publishes curb weight, overall dimensions, track and front/rear weight distribution for cars from 1971. The endpoint is the one free source found that carries kerb weight for vehicles Wikipedia leaves blank. Queried by model year 1995, which returns records stamped MYR 94 and 95; the County Classic record used here is MYR 94. Cross-checked against two cars with known weights (2004 Prius 1,335 kg, 1995 Discovery 1,990 kg) to confirm CW is curb weight in kilograms.

entries.title: Fuel consumption ratings — battery-electric vehicles, model years 2012–2026 (Natural Resources Canada)
entries.publisher: Natural Resources Canada / Government of Canada
entries.note: Publishes a single combined motor output in kilowatts for dual-motor cars, which is exactly what EPA does not: EPA rates each motor separately and Tesla publishes nothing. Metric throughout (kW, km, kWh/100 km, g/km), so no conversion is needed. Canadian-market ratings, so the variant naming follows Canadian trim names.

entries.title: 2004 Toyota Prius 4DR Hatch FWD — NHTSA Canadian Vehicle Specifications
entries.publisher: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
entries.note: Queried by model year 2005; the record is stamped MYR 04. Publishes a 60/40 front/rear weight distribution, and a Canadian-market curb weight of 1,335 kg against the 1,317 kg Wikipedia gives. This is a different market specification, not a contradiction.

entries.title: Volkswagen Kever — RDW Gekentekende Voertuigen (Dutch vehicle registration register)
entries.note: Individual registration records for Dutch-plated 'Kever' (Beetle) cars, not a manufacturer specification. entries.title: Austin Mini / Morris Mini — RDW Gekentekende Voertuigen (Dutch vehicle registration register)
entries.note: Individual registration records for Dutch-plated Austin- and Morris-badged Minis, not a manufacturer specification. Wikipedia gives only a single unattributed model-wide weight range (580-686 kg) for the whole 1959-2000 run, so these dated, badge-specific records are the only per-trim mass figures available and are used structurally where a record's badge and engine size clearly match the trim, with the single-registration caveat stated in each sourceNote. Two 1963 Morris Mini Cooper S records disagree by 22% (535 kg vs 690 kg) despite matching badge/year/displacement, which is why the Cooper S trim here does not use an RDW mass figure.
